title: Product PRD, Roadmap, Pricing and Release Notes - 2026.02
author: Sanjay Rao
content:
Summary

This consolidated product document captures the 2026.02 release PRD, design specifications, roadmap themes for H1-H3 2026, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes. It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and customer-facing teams as a single source of truth for launch and enablement activities.

Audience: Product managers, engineering leads, solutions engineering, sales, and customer success.

1. Product overview

Goal for 2026: Increase adoption of Dedicated and Private deployments by improving out-of-the-box performance, reducing per-token inference cost by at least 20% for common chat and retrieval workloads, and delivering enterprise rollout and observability capabilities.

Core product pillars:
- Performance & Cost: kernel selection improvements, quantization guidance, workload-aware batching.
- Reliability & SLOs: deterministic fallbacks, multi-region routing, stronger canary semantics.
- Developer Experience: API v2, SDK parity, improved quickstarts.
- Enterprise Readiness: BYO-KMS, audit logs, extended observability retention add-ons.

2. PRD (2026.02) - Objectives and success metrics

Primary objective: Ship 2026.02 that includes API v2, Dedicated autoscaling modes, and a Private control plane beta while improving onboarding and integration ergonomics.

Success metrics:
- Dedicated onboarding time target: < 14 days from contract signature to first production traffic.
- Median token latency (512 tokens) on Dedicated P50: < 120ms.
- Targeted per-token cost reduction: >= 20% for chat+retrieval patterns using Optimize recommendations.
- Increase net retention for Dedicated/Private customers by 10% year-over-year.

Requirements (prioritized):
- MUST: Dedicated autoscaling policies: scheduled, utilization, queue-depth.
- MUST: Private control plane supporting VPC peering, private endpoints, and BYO-KMS integration.
- MUST: API v2 responses endpoint supporting sync/async/streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs.
- SHOULD: Console rollout controls including canary percentage ramps and metric-based rollback triggers.
- SHOULD: Initial quantization recommendation engine integrated into Optimize for common open-source models.
- MAY: Beta on-prem packaging for air-gapped customers with a limited hardware matrix.

Non-functional requirements:
- Hosted API availability SLO: 99.9% monthly.
- Dedicated latency SLO: P95 under committed load must be within +20% of baseline.
- Observability retention: enterprise add-on supports token-level traces for 90 days.

Out-of-scope for 2026.02:
- Full multi-cloud private control plane (target 2026.3).
- End-to-end automated model conversion to every quantization format (partial support only).

3. Design specs and API surface (high-level excerpts)

API v2 - Responses endpoint (excerpt):
- POST /v2/responses
- Purpose: Unified endpoint for text generation, chat, streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs.
- Required parameters: model (string), input (string | array of messages), mode ("sync"|"async"|"stream"), max_tokens (int), temperature (float).
- Streaming: chunked SSE (Server-Sent Events) for broad client compatibility.

Example request (sync):
POST /v2/responses
{
  "model": "redwood-1024-chat-v1",
  "input": [{"role":"system","content":"You are Redwood Assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize Q1 roadmap."}],
  "mode": "sync",
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "temperature": 0.2
}

Design trade-offs:
- Single unified endpoint reduces integration surface but increases server-side branching logic.
- SSE chosen for streaming to preserve HTTP/1.1 compatibility across SDKs.
- Fallback order: identical-model fallback -> quantized variant -> hosted fallback. Prioritizes quality then cost.

Serving configuration quick reference:
- batch_window_ms: Max batching delay in ms (default 12, owner: eng-serving-runtime).
- max_batch_size: Max requests per batch (default 128).
- kv_cache_retention: KV cache retention in minutes (default 30).
- quant_profile: Recommended quantization profile (e.g., int8-q4 or fp16).

4. Implementation and rollout plan

Milestones:
- Design & spec complete: 2025-12-15.
- Internal alpha: 2026-01-20.
- Customer beta: 2026-02-28.
- Public GA: 2026-03-15 (2026.02 release).

Dedicated autoscaling rollout playbook (summary):
1) Canary deploy autoscaler in us-west-2 behind a feature flag.
2) Enable queue-depth scaling at 5% synthetic traffic; monitor GPU utilization, queue latency for 72 hours.
3) Expand to 20% internal traffic and invite beta customers.
4) Enable scheduled scaling and publish runbooks.
5) Flip global feature flag after 7-day SLO validation.

Owners:
- Product: Sanjay Rao
- Engineering owner: Priya Patel (eng-platform)
- Runtime owner: Daniel Kim (eng-serving-runtime)
- Beta lead: Maria Gonzalez (customer-success)

5. Roadmap and themes (H1-H3 2026)

Quarterly themes:
- Q1 2026: Dedicated autoscaling, Private control plane beta, API v2 release candidate.
- Q2 2026: Observability retention add-on, rollout controls, SDK parity (Go, Java).
- Q3 2026: Multi-region private control plane, on-prem GA for select customers, advanced Optimize recommendations.

Major epics:
- Dedicated autoscaling and burst capacity.
- Private control plane (VPC, KMS, on-prem).
- API v2 and SDK parity.
- Console rollout and tracing improvements.
- Optimize: model and quantization recommendations.

6. Pricing and packaging guidance

Pricing principles: align with unit economics, keep self-serve simple, enable tiered enterprise contracts for Dedicated and Private.

Reference pricing (list):
- Hosted API: $0.025 per 1K output tokens (public list).
- Dedicated: $40 per GPU-hour (baseline, varies by instance type).
- Private control plane: $2,500 per month (includes control plane + standard support).
- Observability retention add-on: $0.10 per GB-month beyond 30 days.

Packaging bundles:
- Developer: Hosted API, free trial credits, basic telemetry.
- Business: Hosted + limited Dedicated burst, email support, retention trial.
- Enterprise: Reserved Dedicated, Private control plane, premium SLA, TAM, extended retention.

Discount guidance:
- 12-month term: typical 15% discount.
- 36-month term: typical 25% discount.
- Deals > $250k ARR: involve pricing engineering for custom terms.

7. Release notes - 2026.02

Version: 2026.02
Release date: 2026-03-15

Highlights:
- API v2 responses endpoint: unified sync/async/streaming and function calling.
- Dedicated: queue-depth and utilization autoscaling, burst capacity controls, improved scheduling for latency-sensitive loads.
- Private: beta control plane with VPC peering, private endpoints, and BYO-KMS.
- Console: canary rollout controls and per-route cost breakdowns.
- Optimize: initial quantization recommendation engine and model profiles.

Bug fixes and known issues:
- Fixed KV cache spike that could affect P95 under specific synthetic workloads.
- Known: on-prem packaging beta supports a limited hardware set; see onprem-packaging runbook.

Upgrade notes:
- API migration: POST /v2/responses is backwards-compatible for simple generate calls, but function-calling and streaming require explicit mode settings. Review SDK migration guides.
- Dedicated customers: validate autoscaling policies in staging pools prior to production enablement.

8. Risks and mitigation

Top risks:
- Performance regressions during kernel selection changes. Mitigation: progressive canary, traffic mirroring, automated rollback on latency deltas >10%.
- API migration confusion. Mitigation: migration guide, SDK updates, and 60-day legacy compatibility window.

Key monitoring dashboards:
- SLO dashboard: P50/P95 latency, error rates, availability by region.
- Cost dashboard: per-route token spend, quantization utilization, batch efficiency.
- Rollout dashboard: canary metrics, rollback events, and customer incidents.

9. Documentation and enablement required for GA

Docs to publish before GA:
- API v2 spec and quickstarts (Python, JS, Go).
- Dedicated autoscaling runbook and troubleshooting guide.
- Private control plane setup and security checklist.
- Migration guide for legacy responses endpoints.

Sales enablement artifacts:
- Pricing calculator spreadsheet.
- Dedicated onboarding checklist and expected timelines.
- Beta playbook and customer success criteria.

10. Open items and next steps

Open decisions (deadline 2025-12-15):
- Finalize committed GPU-hour pricing tiers for A100 vs H100.
- Confirm observability retention pricing for 180/365-day tiers.

Next actions:
- Finalize ADRs for API v2 and autoscaling (owners: Priya Patel, Daniel Kim).
- Prepare alpha and migration guides (owner: Sanjay Rao).
- Kick off beta with three anchor customers (owner: Maria Gonzalez).
